title: ACT VIII
subtitle: The Hollow Court
rewardRelicDesc: Whenever you play a card, your units gain +1 attack, stacking for the rest of the battle — every mask is a chance to become someone sharper.

jarvMoods: Now, past the Mirror Marsh's last still reeds, still carrying a pane of glass that shows the truth back whether you want it or not.
Now, the Worldmender, standing in a hall of silver masks that all face the same direction when you enter.
Now, wondering what it costs a nobility to forget its own face and call the forgetting a ceremony instead.
Now, past the Reflection's fall, learning that the marsh only ever showed you the water's memory. The Court decided what to do with its own.
courtDesc: The Hollow Court rises past the Mirror Marsh's last reeds, a palace of silver masks and velvet ceremony where every noble answers to a title and none to a name.
This is not a court that forgot out of neglect. It is a court that forgot on purpose, three centuries ago, and built an entire ceremony out of not remembering who used to stand where.
The masks are not a punishment. They are the kindest thing the Court could think to do for itself, once it understood that no one was coming to remind it who it had been.
chamberlainDesc: The Chamberlain has kept the Court's ceremony longer than any noble still wearing a mask, and he has never once needed reminding which gesture erases a name.
He does not rule the Hollow Court the way the Reflection ruled a memory. He stewards it, gesture by gesture, deciding what still deserves to be recognized.

Three centuries of ceremony taught him one thing the Pale Court never had to teach: a face you cannot remember is easier to lose twice. He has not yet decided if the Worldmender counts as a face worth keeping.
priorRunOpenings: The court threshold was already ceremonied when you reached it, same as always — the hall remembers being entered even when it doesn't remember by whom.
You knew the sconce-bearers' step this time. The masked company knew you knowing it.
The name-ledger at the threshold already had your crossing recorded. You are becoming a familiar entry in someone's ceremony.
The Chamberlain's retinue was already standing in the antechamber when you arrived. He does not believe in being surprised twice, either.

panels.title: THE HOLLOW COURT
panels.text:
The court threshold is freshly ceremonied — again.

intro.title: BACKWARDS GLASS
intro.text: The Reflection's stillness gave way behind you, and the pane of glass it left keeps showing you the truth whether you ask for it or not. Past the last still reeds, the road climbs toward a palace of silver masks and velvet ceremony.

intro.title: THE HOLLOW COURT
intro.text: This is not a court that forgot by accident. It is a court that forgot on purpose, three centuries ago, and built an entire ceremony out of not remembering who used to stand where. The masks are not a punishment — they are the kindest thing the Court could think to do for itself.

intro.title: THE CHAMBERLAIN
intro.text: The Court's steward has kept the ceremony longer than any noble still wearing a mask, and he has never once needed reminding which gesture erases a name. He does not rule the Hollow Court. He decides, gesture by gesture, what still deserves to be recognized.

outro.title: THE CHAMBERLAIN'S ACCOUNTING
outro.text: He does not fall like a soldier or a herald. He simply lowers the gesture mid-ceremony, and the hall holds its breath the way it hasn't in three centuries. "I have erased more names than I have kept," he says, "and not one gesture in the ceremony ever told me which was the kinder choice. Tell the Court that, if it still remembers how to listen to anything that isn't its own ritual." He hands you his mask. It is still warm from his face.

outro.title: HOLLOW MASK
outro.text: It is a small thing to have cost a Court its own face — a single mask that sharpens whoever wears it, one gesture at a time. Holding it, you understand the Chamberlain better than his own ceremony ever explained him: forgetting your face is not the same as losing yourself. Not even, it turns out, when the whole Court forgets together.

outro.title: THE WINTER THAT WAITED AHEAD
outro.text: Past the Court's last antechamber, the corridors give way to a season the void kept in storage — a winter Amarath never got to have, waiting three centuries for someone to release it. Somewhere beyond the last silver mask, the cold is already deciding who it was owed to.

court-threshold.label: The Court Threshold
court-threshold.description: Where the Mirror Marsh's last reeds give way to the Hollow Court's first ceremonial gate.

the-hollow-corridor.label: The Hollow Corridor
the-hollow-corridor.description: A corridor lined with masks that all turn to face whoever walks it.

the-silver-antechamber.label: The Silver Antechamber
the-silver-antechamber.description: An antechamber garrisoned like it still expects a ceremony nobody scheduled.

the-name-ledger.label: The Name Ledger
the-name-ledger.description: A Court clerk tallying every name still allowed to be spoken aloud.

eventConfig.title: The Name Ledger
eventConfig.description: A clerk keeps the tally at a lectern draped in Court velvet, marking every name against a ceremony three centuries deep. She does not ask why you're crossing. She only asks whether you intend to be recorded.

pools.label: Pay the ledger's toll (lose 6 HP, gain a rare card)
pools.consequence: Every name recorded costs a little of your own. You receive a rare card.

pools.label: Take the clerk's ceremony-oil (gain 60 crystals)
pools.consequence: Oil set aside for a ceremony that never quite runs short. You gain 60 crystals.

pools.label: Rest at the ledger post's brazier (heal 10 HP)
pools.consequence: The brazier holds the chill back better than it has any right to. You heal 10 HP.

pools.label: Leave the ledger uncounted
pools.consequence: You leave the clerk to her tally.

the-court-hearth.label: The Court Hearth
the-court-hearth.description: A ceremonial hearth, kept lit for attendants coming off a cold vigil.

the-sealed-archive-gate.label: The Sealed Archive Gate
the-sealed-archive-gate.description: A gate posting ceremony orders that read like they were never meant for a hall this ordinary.

eventConfig.title: The Sealed Archive Gate
eventConfig.description: The writ nailed to the gate names every noble in the hall and the ceremony each is due to perform. It is signed by the Chamberlain, countersigned by nobody the Court still remembers, and dated the same day the vanguard crossed the Marches.

pools.label: Read the sealed archive writ (lose 6 HP, gain a rare card)
pools.consequence: Every name named costs you something to read past. You receive a rare card.

pools.label: Take the archive's oil cache (gain 70 crystals)
pools.consequence: A cache nobody in this hall was ever going to collect. You gain 70 crystals.

pools.label: Rest behind the archive's seals (heal 8 HP)
pools.consequence: Quieter than a ceremonial hall has any right to be. You heal 8 HP.

pools.label: Leave the writ unread
pools.consequence: Some orders are better left uncounted. You move on.

the-chamberlains-cart.label: The Chamberlain's Cart
the-chamberlains-cart.description: A trading cart parked in a hall that hasn't seen open trade in centuries.

the-masked-company.label: The Masked Company
the-masked-company.description: A file of Court soldiers holding formation behind silver masks that never once slip.

mem-c2act8-1.label: Memory Fragment
mem-c2act8-1.description: A founding charter of the Court's first masked ceremony.

the-hollow-line.label: The Hollow Line
the-hollow-line.description: A line of courtiers who never got new orders when the ceremony forgot their names.

the-deep-corridors.label: The Deep Corridors
the-deep-corridors.description: Corridors deep enough that even the candlelight stops following.

the-last-ceremony.label: The Last Ceremony
the-last-ceremony.description: The final ceremonial hall before the Chamberlain's own chamber.

the-final-antechamber.label: The Final Antechamber
the-final-antechamber.description: The last antechamber before the Chamberlain's own hall. Someone has already lit its sconces.

mem-c2act8-2.label: Memory Fragment
mem-c2act8-2.description: A courtier's log from the night the inner ceremony first sealed its own gate.

chamberlain-node.label: The Chamberlain
chamberlain-node.description: Every ceremony in the Hollow Court ends here, before a steward who decides what still deserves a name.
bossDialogue: You crossed the Mirror Marsh, Worldmender. The Reflection gave you a world remembered. I give you a Court that forgot its own face and dressed the wound in silver instead.

Three centuries in the void, and not one noble in this hall recalls what they looked like before the Fracture erased Amarath. I gave them masks so the not-knowing would have a shape. You are the first thing in three centuries that has made any of them want to take one off.
The Court does not ask me to defend this ceremony. It only asks that I decide, gesture by gesture, what still deserves a name. Let's begin.

the-inner-gate.label: The Inner Gate
the-inner-gate.description: A second ceremonial gate, deeper in the Court than any outsider was ever meant to reach.

the-veiled-corridor.label: The Veiled Corridor
the-veiled-corridor.description: A corridor hung with veils instead of masks, for a ceremony the outer court never learned.

the-gilded-antechamber.label: The Gilded Antechamber
the-gilded-antechamber.description: An antechamber gilded for a Chamberlain who has not received a real guest in three centuries.

the-shrouded-flank.label: The Shrouded Flank
the-shrouded-flank.description: A flanking hall kept shrouded since the ceremony that named it stopped being spoken of.

the-second-ledger.label: The Second Ledger
the-second-ledger.description: A ledger kept apart from the outer court, recording names the first ledger was never shown.

eventConfig.title: The Second Ledger
eventConfig.description: This ledger sits behind a door the outer clerks do not have keys to, recording names the Court decided the first ledger should never see. Every entry is a name that was recorded twice, once in error.

pools.label: Read the second ledger (lose 6 HP, gain a rare card)
pools.consequence: A record within a record costs more to read. You receive a rare card.

pools.label: Take the clerk's second cache (gain 70 crystals)
pools.consequence: A cache the first ledger never accounted for. You gain 70 crystals.

pools.label: Rest behind the second door (heal 9 HP)
pools.consequence: Quieter than a hall that keeps two ledgers has any right to be. You heal 9 HP.

pools.label: Leave the second ledger unread
pools.consequence: Some records are better left double-uncounted. You move on.

the-vigil-hearth.label: The Vigil Hearth
the-vigil-hearth.description: A second hearth, kept for attendants who serve a ceremony nobody outside ever hears of.

the-sealed-inner-gate.label: The Sealed Inner Gate
the-sealed-inner-gate.description: A second sealed gate, posting orders for a ceremony the outer court was never told existed.

eventConfig.title: The Sealed Inner Gate
eventConfig.description: The writ on this gate is signed by the Chamberlain twice — once in the hand the outer court knows, once in a hand nobody has seen in three hundred years. Both signatures agree on every word.

pools.label: Read the inner writ (lose 6 HP, gain a rare card)
pools.consequence: Two signatures cost more to read past than one. You receive a rare card.

pools.label: Take the inner gate's cache (gain 70 crystals)
pools.consequence: A cache nobody past the outer gate was ever going to collect. You gain 70 crystals.

pools.label: Rest behind the inner seals (heal 8 HP)
pools.consequence: Quieter than a twice-sealed gate has any right to be. You heal 8 HP.

pools.label: Leave the inner writ unread
pools.consequence: Some orders are better left twice-uncounted. You move on.

the-inner-cart.label: The Inner Court's Cart
the-inner-cart.description: A second trading cart, further in than the Chamberlain admits any cart has reason to be.

the-silver-company.label: The Silver Company
the-silver-company.description: A second file of Court soldiers, masked in silver finer than anything the outer court wears.

the-veiled-line.label: The Veiled Line
the-veiled-line.description: A line of courtiers veiled rather than masked, for a rank the outer ceremony never named.

the-gilt-corridors.label: The Gilt Corridors
the-gilt-corridors.description: Corridors gilded over the same silver the outer court never sees polished.

the-last-veil.label: The Last Veil
the-last-veil.description: The final veiled hall before the Chamberlain receives anyone at all.
